classes.DETERMINISTIC: one known frame, one target frame; the difficulty is carried by vocabulary
classes.SPLIT: one known frame, two or more target frames chosen by a trigger present somewhere in the known sentence (the trigger may be non-local to the cut)
classes.INVERSION: the shape mirrors — constituent order reorganises, walked in the reverse direction
classes.ERASURE: the target (English) is simpler and drops a distinction the known side marks; convergence, harmless under one-directional ZUT
classes.MINT: one known frame, two or more target realisations, and the selector is not in the known sentence and cannot be put into any cut of it, because the known language does not encode the information; the selector lives outside the sentence — discourse state, time of speaking, referent status. [SPEC:worker] name MINT taken from frame-zut.md's 'minting from nothing'; fallback name UNCUED if the collision with the layer verb ('phrases MINT') is unwanted

mint_vs_split_test: hand a competent bilingual the complete known sentence in isolation: if the sentence still underdetermines the target form the row is MINT; if the sentence determines it (even when the chunk alone does not) the row is SPLIT

reversal_law.statement: the reverse table cannot be computed from the forward table; class membership is re-derived per row, and depends on where the information lives, not on the forward label

forward_to_reverse.DETERMINISTIC: DETERMINISTIC unless the forward mapping was many-to-one in disguise
forward_to_reverse.SPLIT: usually ERASURE (converges); can re-fork on the English side — see carrier_condition
forward_to_reverse.INVERSION: INVERSION, often carrying a new sentence-cued fork of its own
forward_to_reverse.ERASURE: SPLIT where the known sentence still contains a selector; MINT where it does not

reversal_law.carrier_condition: a convergence is only free if the cut carries the matrix: que+SUBJUNCTIVE re-expands as 'you to VP' after quiero but 'you'll VP' after espero, so the matrix verb must ride inside the chunk (live cuts eng_for_spa S0015L01 'quiero que hables', S0149L01 'espero que termines')

recut_fixes: do-support from spa: cut the ¿...? wrapper into the unit (¿ → did, S0032L01)
do-support from zho: 吗 is a word; X吗 → do X? deterministic once cut
infinitive-vs-future after volition/hope: cut the matrix verb into the chunk (quiero que hables / espero que termines, never bare que+subjunctive)
subject pronouns from spa: morphology carries person; cut mints pronoun+verb together (estoy → I'm)
past from zho when a time word exists: upchunk it (我昨天想问 → I wanted to ask … yesterday)
cut_cost.residue_fix: not cutting — authoring: differentiate the known prompt (add 昨天/已经/这个 so the choice is cued) or teach by contrast pair inside one basket; both are basket/authoring operations. Forwards: re-cut the unit. Backwards: re-cut where a trigger exists, re-author where none does.

reverse_frame_zut.rule: for each phrase P in a basket for seed S: for each applicable mapping M — if M is SPLIT, P's known sentence must contain M's trigger for the outcome P's target realises (trigger may be non-local to the cut), else VIOLATION; if M is MINT, either P's known side carries an authored-in differentiator for the outcome, or the basket contains a contrast phrase with minimally different known side realising a different outcome, else VIOLATION (the learner is drilled into a guess with no way to ever be right)
reverse_frame_zut.course_level_corollary: a MINT's default outcome must be established before its contrast arrives — the basket that first carries the marked outcome must bring the contrast pair or a differentiated prompt
reverse_frame_zut.tooling: tools/frame-layer/reverse-zut-scan.cjs finds known-side divergence groups in any eng_for_X lego layer (repeatable measurement); the basket-level checker needs the phrase layer and known-side matchers — NOT YET BUILT
